title: 1 Timothy Bible Quiz - Chapter 1
description: Ten questions on 1 Timothy 1: the charge to stay at Ephesus, the purpose of the law, and the mercy shown to the writer himself.

questions.text: How does the writer address Timothy in verse 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 writes to Timothy as “my true child in faith”, with grace, mercy, and peace.

answers.text: As his true child in faith
As his brother in the flesh
As his servant in the Lord

questions.text: In which city was Timothy to stay?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says that, as he was going into Macedonia, he urged Timothy to stay at Ephesus.

questions.text: What were they not to pay attention to, according to verse 4?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which cause disputes.

questions.text: What is the goal of this command?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says the goal of the command is love, out of a pure heart and a good conscience and sincere faith.

questions.text: On what condition is the law good, according to verse 8?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says we know that the law is good, if a person uses it lawfully.

answers.text: If it is read in the assembly
If a person uses it lawfully
If it is kept without fault

questions.text: For whom is law not made, according to verse 9?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate.

questions.text: What does the writer say he used to be?
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says he used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent, but obtained mercy.

questions.text: What is the faithful saying in verse 15?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says the saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.

answers.text: Christ Jesus came to judge the nations
Christ Jesus came to save sinners
The law was given through angels
Every creature of God is good

questions.text: How is the King described in verse 17?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 gives honor and glory to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise.

questions.text: Who are named in verse 20 as delivered to Satan so that they might be taught not to blaspheme?
questions.explanation: Verse 20 names Hymenaeus and Alexander, of those who thrust away faith and a good conscience.
